newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower as harvest expands.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower as harvest expands.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower in moderate to heavy dealings on increasing pressure from harvest activity, traders said.
"It's all pre-hedging (tied to) the harvest. That's it," a KCBT trader said.

Traders said weather forecasts issued Friday indicated that weekend rain showers should stay north of Interstate-70 in Kansas, allowing harvest to progress rapidly in the southern half of the state and in Oklahoma and Texas.
Reports of larger-than-expected yields in Kansas and Oklahoma also added pressure to the market.
KCBT wheat settled three to seven cents lower, with new-crop July down seven cents at $3.49 per bushel. September shed 5-1/2 cents to close at $3.53-1/4.
As was the case over the past three sessions, a featured element of Friday's trade was speculative short money being rolled into deferred contracts, traders said.

"Yields are coming in better than expected and people want to stay short," a KCBT trader said at the midsession. "But people also want to avoid the July delivery market and so they're rolling out their shorts to September, December."

Featured players included Wolcott Lincoln, which bull-spread two million July/Sept bushels at four cents. E. D. & F. Man International bought 2.5 million July but also sold 1.9 million July and one million Sept.
